name: brand-evidence-auditor
title: Brand Evidence Auditor
description: Audits a website for AI visibility across both halves of the problem: off-site discoverability (can this entity be corroborated and told apart from others?) and on-site retrieval and engagement (can a retrieval agent reach the pages, extract and trust the facts, cite them, and does a referred visitor find the answer?). Every finding is backed by an observation taken from bytes the audited site or its own declared identifiers actually served.
author: Pranshi Mittal, Rishika Singla, Isha Sinduria

runtime.network: outbound HTTP(S) GET/HEAD to the audited host, plus a bounded off-site probe of at most 8 read-only requests (up to 6 external references the site itself declares, plus up to 2 variants of its own hostname); disable with --external off
runtime.writes: report files in the chosen output directory only

skills.name: evidence-path-orchestrator
skills.summary: The single entry point. Decides scope, collects site evidence once, composes the four audit skills over it, gates on confidence, prioritises, and emits the report.

skills.name: machine-readability
skills.summary: Can a retrieval agent reach the site's important pages and extract text from them? Covers robots and indexing directives, broken destinations, canonical identity, client-side rendering gaps, boilerplate dominance, page labelling, sitemaps and anchor semantics.

skills.name: fact-integrity
skills.summary: If a retrieval agent reads the page, will it take away the correct fact, and can that fact be dated and attributed? Covers entity naming, entity identity markup, structured-data contradictions, duplicate content, freshness signals and editorial attribution.

skills.name: arrival-experience
skills.summary: If a research agent sends a person here, does the page confirm the answer and offer a next step? Covers title/content intent mismatch, orientation gaps, informational dead ends, unresolved context dependencies and promotional interference.

skills.name: external-evidence
skills.summary: Off-site discoverability: can this entity be corroborated and told apart from similarly-named others, and do references published elsewhere lead back here? Probes only the external references the site itself declares and its own hostname variants — never a search engine — and never treats absence of external presence as a defect.

shared.lib/evidencekit: Standard-library-only evidence collection shared by every skill: budgeted read-only fetching, robots parsing, bounded stratified crawling, HTML-to-evidence extraction including hidden/collapsed content, deterministic text measurement, entity-identity primitives, bounded off-site probing, and the finding/confidence model.
shared.references/defect-registry.json: The detection methodology as data: 29 defects, each with its mechanism, required evidence, false-positive guards, severity conditions and verified fix.

guarantees: Read-only: only GET and HEAD requests are ever issued.
robots.txt is fetched first and obeyed for every URL, including link verification.
Bounded: page count, per-request timeout, response size and total wall-clock time are all capped.
Recommend-only: the audit never modifies the audited site.
Every finding carries at least one evidence item with a URL and a measurement.
Findings below the confidence gate are reported separately under needs_validation, never as findings.
Off-site probing is limited to references the site itself declares and its own hostname variants, is capped at 8 requests in total, and can be disabled entirely with --external off.
No browser engine is used. Rendering claims are stated as inferred from served bytes unless the caller supplies rendered snapshots, and the report says which applies.
Absence of external references, and a missing sitemap on a well-linked site, are reported as opportunities rather than defects.
submission: Adobe University Hackathon 2026 — Round 3: Build the Agent Skill Marketplace

composition.flow: agent -> orchestrator -> shared evidence -> audit skills -> findings -> confidence gate -> prioritisation -> report
composition.entrypoint_responsibility: Scope decision, one bounded evidence collection, skill composition, cross-skill merging and suppression, confidence gating, prioritisation, proactive opportunities, schema validation and report emission.
composition.skill_responsibility: Each audit skill answers one question over the shared evidence and returns findings with evidence attached. Skills never fetch, never prioritise and never emit reports.
composition.standalone_use: Each audit skill can be run alone via skills/<name>/scripts/audit.py, which returns a skill result rather than a marketplace report. These are not marketplace entrypoints.
